Appalachian State Mountaineers.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that Dowell Loggains has coached offense in some capacity his whole career, and that he coached with Matt Hasselbeck at the Titans in the early 2010s.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.oc: Mike Anthony, who was an assistant under Kendal Briles at multiple stops.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.dc: DJ Smith, who did good work at Missouri under Eli Drinkwitz.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.oc_status: New — the guide records Anthony's arrival and a new scheme, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.offensive_scheme: Not named, but its direction is stated: the guide expects the pace to rise, noting Anthony was an assistant under Kendal Briles at multiple stops, and records a new scheme alongside a rebuilt quarterback room.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.tempo: Expected to increase, and tied to a structural edge: App State plays at the highest elevation east of the Mississippi River in FBS, and the guide says using it makes a great deal of sense if the new-look offense can play fast enough to.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide's analytical case for the new quarterbacks is mobility — Henry Hasselbeck and Malachi Singleton are more mobile than last year's options and should add explosiveness.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.qb_development: Addressed as a judgement on the previous room. The guide reads last season's usage as a verdict — AJ Swann and JJ Kohl attempted nearly the same number of passes and three other quarterbacks took reps, which it calls fair evidence Loggains was not enamoured with any of them — and records the position being rebuilt through the portal around Malachi Singleton from Purdue, Henry Hasselbeck from UCLA and Tommy Ulatowski from Kent State.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 5 returning starters, totalling 7.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, with a new scheme arriving alongside him.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.prior_school: Missouri under Eli Drinkwitz for DJ Smith, and the guide notes Drinkwitz coached the Mountaineers to 12-1 in 2019 before leaving ahead of the bowl game. Kendal Briles' staffs are Mike Anthony's reference point. On the roster the guide records Malachi Singleton from Purdue, Henry Hasselbeck from UCLA, Tommy Ulatowski from Kent State, Ja'Quez Cross from Arkansas State and Chris Lofton from Gardner-Webb.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.portal_recruiting: The central optimistic case. Per 247Sports, App State signed the second-ranked transfer portal class — including several new quarterback options — plus the top freshman class in the conference. The guide draws a contrast with the previous staff, saying Shawn Clark had some good seasons but was not bringing in much athleticism, and rates this roster considerably stronger.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.vsin_assessment: Optimism built on recruiting, with the defense named as the decisive unit. The guide rests its year-two case on the portal and freshman classes and on Loggains' offensive background, states outright that it believes the offense will be better and that a more dual-threat quarterback may be a game-changer, and grades the defense a major disappointment in conference play — 33 points and 450 yards allowed per game, outgained by 1.1 yards per carry, and a 2-7 Sun Belt record. It labels that unit simultaneously the most important and most unknown on the team.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.strengths: The second-ranked portal class nationally and the top freshman class in the conference, a coordinator hire from the Kendal Briles tree expected to raise tempo, a returning defensive coordinator the guide credits with good work at Missouri, the leading tackler back, and a genuine home-field structural edge in elevation.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.concerns: Only five returning starters, an offense that managed 5.4 yards per play and 24.2 points per game against a programme benchmark of six yards per play, a quarterback room rebuilt entirely from the portal, and a defense that conceded 33 points per game in conference play.
Appalachian State Mountaineers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 5.67 wins, with a stated belief the team can overachieve after two down seasons.

Arkansas State Red Wolves.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide frames Butch Jones' Arkansas State tenure as a rebuild that needed a couple of seasons to pick up the pieces in Jonesboro after COVID and the end of Blake Anderson's tenure.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.oc: Garrett Altman, who spent the last two years coaching Diego Pavia at Vanderbilt.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.dc: Griff McCarley, entering his second year.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.oc_status: New — the guide records Altman's arrival and says a fresh installation is going in anyway, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.offensive_scheme: Not named, but characterised by the coordinator's pedigree: the guide traces Altman from playing at TCU a decade ago to an analyst role at New Mexico State when Pavia was there, calls him instrumental in every phase of that quarterback's development, and supplies the supporting fact that Vanderbilt led the nation at 7.47 yards per play last season.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the unit allowing 6.1 yards per play, better than the prior 6.9.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.run_pass: Addressed through a sceptical reading of last season's volume: a career-best 3,361 passing yards came with a Sun Belt-leading 501 attempts, while the team fell from 4.2 yards per carry across the previous two seasons to 3.8.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.qb_development: Addressed as a coordinator's record rather than a programme's. The guide's case for Altman is recency and pedigree through Diego Pavia's development, and it lists the whole quarterback field with a distinct reason to believe in each: the ex-Commodores already know Altman's philosophy, Trey Owens probably has the most untapped upside, and Ethan Crawford knows the returning skill players.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 9.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, and the guide treats the timing as convenient rather than disruptive — a fresh installation is going in anyway.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.prior_school: Vanderbilt for Altman, and the connection reaches the roster: Drew Dickey and Jeremy St-Hilaire sat behind Pavia there. TCU and New Mexico State are his earlier reference points. The guide also records Trey Owens as a four-star Texas prospect committed to UT who never saw the field.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.portal_recruiting: Addressed at quarterback, where the whole room was rebuilt, with two arrivals who already know the coordinator's philosophy.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.vsin_assessment: Coaching credited by a specific result, with the transition read as double-edged. The guide singles out a 5-3 Sun Belt record despite a ghastly -11 turnover margin as evidence of coaching, then argues the quarterback departure cuts both ways — in its favour, the running game dropped off precipitously and Jaylen Raynor had a lot to do with it at 2.7 yards per carry, and a new coordinator means a fresh installation regardless; against it, Raynor leaves at the same time as all-time leading receiver Corey Rucker. On defense it credits Griff McCarley with an immediate pass-rush jump from 19 sacks to 39, while doubting repeatability with a completely new line.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with a 5-3 conference record despite a -11 turnover margin, a coordinator hire with direct involvement in Diego Pavia's development from a Vanderbilt offense that led the nation in yards per play, defensive-coordinator continuity after a sack total that doubled, and returning skill players including a 73-catch receiver.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.concerns: Essentially zero quarterback experience on the roster, the simultaneous loss of the quarterback and the all-time leading receiver, a completely new defensive line with essentially everyone who had more than one sack gone, and a defense that despite ranking sixth nationally in sacks per game forced only seven interceptions and allowed a 68.4% completion rate.
Arkansas State Red Wolves.betting: The guide prefers a different market entirely — betting Over the game total on a weekly basis — with an explicit timing argument tied to the coaching change: if a quarterback emerges the books will catch up, but if Altman picks the right player or players from the outset there is an edge before the market adjusts. Projection is 6.36 wins.

Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.previous_hc_experience: Yes, at a programme in transition. The Coaching Carousel records that after overseeing Missouri State's transition from FCS to FBS, Ryan Beard took the Bears to a bowl game in their first season as a Conference USA member, though he did not coach in it because Coastal Carolina came calling. It records six seasons at Missouri State, first as defensive coordinator under Bobby Petrino and then as head coach when Petrino left to be Texas A&M's OC, and identifies Beard as Petrino's son-in-law and a former Western Kentucky defensive back.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.oc: Not addressed by name. The guide records that Beard brought his coordinators with him from Missouri State.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.dc: LD Scott, who follows Beard from Missouri State.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.dc_status: New — the guide records LD Scott taking over, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, though the Coaching Carousel identifies a stated coaching strength: Beard has been very successful in getting his players to get to the quarterback, and it sets that against Coastal having only 19 sacks last season with 80 sack yards, the seventh-fewest — offering it as food for thought.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.qb_development: Addressed through familiarity. Deuce Bailey was Jacob Clark's backup at Missouri State and got his chance when Clark was hurt; the guide treats Beard's familiarity with him as an advantage, compares him to Samari Collier's spark for Coastal last season, observes that a dual-threat quarterback looks like a luxury in this conference, and judges the talent level at the position looks a lot better.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.continuity: None on paper. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 1. The guide separately credits Beard with sideline continuity because he brought his coordinators with him.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.staff_turnover: Complete at Coastal but internally continuous for the incoming staff — Beard brought his coordinators from Missouri State, which the guide credits, while leaving the buy-in question open: how quickly will all the newcomers adapt?
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.prior_school: Missouri State, comprehensively — Beard, his coordinators, LD Scott and quarterback Deuce Bailey. The guide also records Trever Jackson from Arkansas, JUCO transfer Tre Guerra whose offer list it gives as Texas Tech, Kentucky, Florida State, LSU and Virginia, and Daughtry Richardson, who played one game at Florida State before transferring to FAU.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.portal_recruiting: The scale of the rebuild is the central fact: roughly 60 new players, including a conference-high 42 transfers per 247Sports. The guide's supporting evidence for its multi-year read is eligibility — all the quarterbacks Beard brought in, and virtually all the skill players, have eligibility beyond this season.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.vsin_assessment: A teardown the guide endorses, at a stated cost to this season. It recounts that when Jamey Chadwell left for Liberty, Coastal hired Tim Beck, and many in the college football gambling community felt it was one of the biggest coaching downgrades in the nation — 8-5 in year one, then back-to-back losing seasons that sent him packing. Its reasoning concludes that the programme was unquestionably trending the wrong way under Beck, that a teardown to the studs makes the most sense, and that Beard's Missouri State record as a programme builder supports it — Coastal needs a refresh and will get one, probably at the expense of this season's record. Projection is 4.86 wins.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.strengths: A head coach who built a programme through an FCS-to-FBS transition and reached a bowl in its first Conference USA season, coordinators who came with him, a quarterback he already knows, a defensive coaching strength in pass rush that matches Coastal's clearest weakness, and a roster built with eligibility beyond this season.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.concerns: A Stability Score of 1 with roughly 60 new players and a conference-high 42 transfers, an offensive line the guide calls easily the most questionable position group with none of the members having played together, a Missouri State precedent of 52 sacks allowed, and a defense that conceded 33.1 points and 5.5 yards per carry in conference play.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.carousel_summary: Adam Burke records the sequence and the lineage. After overseeing Missouri State's transition from FCS to FBS, Beard took the Bears to a bowl game in their first season as a member of Conference USA — he didn't coach in it, as Coastal Carolina came calling and he hit the ground running in Conway. Burke notes Beard is Bobby Petrino's son-in-law and was at Missouri State for six seasons, first as the DC under Petrino and then as head coach when Petrino went to be the OC at Texas A&M. He then makes the point that ties the hire to the job: Beard, who was a defensive back at Western Kentucky, has been very successful in getting his players to get to the quarterback — and Coastal Carolina only had 19 sacks last season, their 80 sack yards the seventh-fewest. Just some food for thought.

Georgia Southern Eagles.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide beyond Georgia Southern itself. The guide records Clay Helton reaching a bowl in each of his four seasons and just claiming his first bowl win to cap a 7-6 season.
Georgia Southern Eagles.dc: Mike Mutz, in from Stephen F. Austin.
Georgia Southern Eagles.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Georgia Southern Eagles.dc_status: New — the guide flags a new defensive coordinator, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Georgia Southern Eagles.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Georgia Southern Eagles.offensive_scheme: Named as a spread, and the guide treats the switch as the defining coaching decision here: Helton moved the Eagles from an option offense to a spread, which has produced productive quarterback play in relative terms. It supports this with the record book — JC French leads the programme with just 5,882 yards and Kyle Vantrease, from one season in 2022, is third with 4,253.
Georgia Southern Eagles.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's case for Mutz is his Stephen F. Austin defense, which generated a great many negative plays and takeaways.
Georgia Southern Eagles.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Georgia Southern Eagles.qb_development: Attributed to the scheme rather than to individual coaching. The guide argues the scheme itself will produce numbers, presents Max Johnson as capable of a Vantrease-like season or better after playing at LSU, Texas A&M and North Carolina across seven seasons, notes the obvious joke about his longevity, then makes the serious point that schools keep paying him to come.
Georgia Southern Eagles.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 8.
Georgia Southern Eagles.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, and the guide sets it against a stated institutional argument for stability: avoiding a coach's buyout and the recurring cost of hiring new staff and enticing new recruits has plenty of perks.
Georgia Southern Eagles.prior_school: Stephen F. Austin for Mutz. On the roster the guide records Max Johnson from LSU, Texas A&M and North Carolina, Ashton Hollis from Illinois and Andre Greene from Virginia.
Georgia Southern Eagles.portal_recruiting: Addressed at receiver, where the top five pass-catchers are gone and the guide names portal candidates to replace them.
Georgia Southern Eagles.vsin_assessment: Predictability valued, with the defense as the upside lever. The guide's framing is the value of an athletic department that knows what to expect, and it sets the financial argument for stability alongside Helton's four bowls in four seasons. Its conclusion is bullish: a really high ceiling, possibly higher than anyone expects if Mutz can fix the defense — which it calls one of its biggest overlays.
Georgia Southern Eagles.strengths: Four straight bowl appearances and a first bowl win, offensive-coordinator continuity, a scheme change already made that the guide credits with productive quarterback play, a very experienced quarterback in his final year of eligibility, a deep skill group, and a defensive hire whose previous unit generated negative plays and takeaways.
Georgia Southern Eagles.concerns: A new defensive coordinator inheriting a pass rush that produced only 12 sacks in 13 games, the loss of the all-time leading passer and all five top pass-catchers including an NFL-calibre 1,000-yard receiver, and only nine returning starters.
Georgia Southern Eagles.betting: The guide calls this one of its biggest overlays, with a projection of 5.49 wins putting the alt Over 5.5 in play — and its stated condition is coaching: the ceiling rises if Mutz can fix the defense, in which case it projects the Eagles' first defense allowing fewer than six yards per play since 2020.

Georgia State Panthers.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as head-coaching experience. The guide records that Dell McGee has spent a lot of time in Georgia, including several seasons with the Bulldogs as running backs coach and run game coordinator, and that his reputation as a recruiter was expected to raise the talent level.
Georgia State Panthers.dc: Co-defensive coordinators Cam Clark, who was working with quarterbacks at Duke and was a high school defensive coordinator before that, and John Haneline, whose Youngstown State defense allowed 31 points per game last season. Travis Pearson left for a UFL job.
Georgia State Panthers.oc_status: Returning — the guide records Hue Jackson back, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Georgia State Panthers.dc_status: New — the guide records the co-defensive coordinators as new, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Georgia State Panthers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Georgia State Panthers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Georgia State Panthers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide isolates second halves as the failure: Georgia State allowed the most second-half points per game in the country at 20.8, essentially outscored 21-8 after the interval, which it attributes to McGee and his staff failing to adjust and to insufficient depth.
Georgia State Panthers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide notes a mobile quarterback helped limit sacks to 18 while the team still regressed in yards per carry.
Georgia State Panthers.personnel: Addressed as a size concern: all the running backs are under six feet, and leading returning receiver Grant Hollier, one of the few big bodies, had just 21 catches.
Georgia State Panthers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide tests Cameran Brown against outcomes rather than statistics — the Panthers lost all three games in which he passed for 200-plus yards, averaging 25 points in them while the defense allowed 41, 41 and 38 — and notes that even when he played well it did not seem to matter.
Georgia State Panthers.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinators change. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 12, against a 1-11 record.
Georgia State Panthers.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive side, and the guide records the conditions that prompted it — coordinator Travis Pearson left for a UFL job — while calling the two replacements underwhelming hires. It reads the changes as McGee probably needing a decent season to save his job.
Georgia State Panthers.prior_school: Georgia, where McGee spent several seasons as running backs coach and run game coordinator. Duke and Youngstown State are the new coordinators' reference points. On the roster the guide records Power Four offensive line transfers from Florida, Georgia, Michigan, Georgia Tech and Oklahoma State.
Georgia State Panthers.portal_recruiting: Held against the recruiting reputation. The guide credits McGee with the lone freshman graded four-star by 247Sports, offensive lineman Maxwell Robinson, plus five Power Four offensive line transfers — with the qualification that they played sparingly or not at all. Its structural conclusion is that a coach like McGee makes sense on paper but lacks the big NIL budget that this kind of head coach requires.
Georgia State Panthers.vsin_assessment: Blunt, and careful to separate the roles. The guide's verdict on the tenure is that the Dell McGee era in Atlanta has not gone well: 4-20 overall and 1-15 in Sun Belt play, shut out of Sun Belt wins last season with the lone victory over FCS Murray State. It grants the hire was imaginative and offers injuries as a mitigating factor, then separates the roles explicitly — McGee has not proven to be a college-level head coach, though it accepts him as a position coach and absolutely as a recruiter. It adds market evidence: the team is 5-18-1 ATS over the past two seasons, falling short of virtually no expectations. On the new coordinators it agrees a new crop of players is probably not a bad thing while calling the two hires underwhelming.
Georgia State Panthers.strengths: A head coach the guide accepts absolutely as a recruiter and as a position coach, offensive-coordinator continuity, a returning quarterback with a 13-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio, a four-star freshman offensive lineman, and five Power Four offensive line transfers.
Georgia State Panthers.concerns: A 4-20 overall and 1-15 conference record, the most second-half points allowed in the country which the guide attributes to failures to adjust, two coordinator hires it calls underwhelming, the loss of a 1,000-yard receiver and the leading rusher, 18 sacks in back-to-back seasons with 37.8 points allowed, and no NIL budget to match the head coach's recruiting profile.
Georgia State Panthers.betting: The guide's coaching-linked market evidence is that Georgia State is 5-18-1 ATS over the past two seasons, falling short of virtually no expectations.
